clue.text: He composed music, limiting volume: heavens!

indicators.note: limiting means closing in on something, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: a strain is a passage or snatch of music
the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: A composer's music is cramped for loudness, and someone cries out in exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He composed music' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'He composed'; 'music' is the strain that holds V.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky was the Russian-born creator of The Rite of Spring, a man who wrote scores.

clue.text: Most unusual ways to limit travel over wide area

indicators.note: to limit means to hem something in, so the ways go round the travelling

parts.note: ST is short for street, and two streets are two ways, one on each side
to range is to roam over a wide area

explanation.surface: Odd methods for restricting long-distance journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ways' supplies two ST abbreviations, one at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of strange: oddest, most peculiar.

clue.text: Sounded impolite and cross

indicators.note: Sounded says the word for impolite is heard rather than written

parts.note: impolite means rude

explanation.surface: Someone was audibly rude and angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry; it is the noun, a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen.

clue.text: Energy: see it displayed in European country

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references

indicators.note: displayed in says one piece is set out within another

parts.note: Italy is a European country

explanation.surface: Vigour can be observed in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'see' comes from the Latin vide used in footnotes; 'displayed in' places the pronoun just before the country's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitality is liveliness and vigour, a synonym for energy.

clue.text: Wealthy person who has secured a billion?

definitions.text: Wealthy person who has secured a billion?

indicators.note: who has secured says the first piece holds the next inside it

parts.note: a nob is a rich or upper-class person

explanation.surface: A rich man who has made his first billion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: a NOB holding A B.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a person of great wealth, originally one who made a fortune in India.

clue.text: Girl crashing in a kart

indicators.note: crashing suggests the go-kart's letters smashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman has an accident while go-karting.
explanation.definitionFit: Katrina is a female first name.

clue.text: Elegant ambassador briefly back in town

parts.note: chic means elegant
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A stylish diplomat returns to a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction for the diplomat; it is the STERN of a boat, docked of its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichester is a cathedral city in West Sussex, England, so a fair example of a town.

clue.text: Extract from Gene Vincent show

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clip from a Gene Vincent concert, the American rock'n'roll singer.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to display or make evident, a synonym for show as a verb.

clue.text: With first part of holiday finished, left transport terminal

indicators.note: first part of picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: something finished is over
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Once the holiday's start is done, someone departs from the travel terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoverport is a terminal for hovercraft passengers, a kind of transport depot.

clue.text: Snack's sharp taste?

definitions.meaning: the pungent kick of a strong flavour

explanation.surface: A light meal with a tangy flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bite is both a mouthful of food and the tang of a sharp flavour.

clue.text: Thrashin' English boxer, perhaps

parts.note: thrashing is caning, and with its final g clipped as in the clue it loses that letter

explanation.surface: A fighter is giving an Englishman a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a fighter; it is the dog breed. The apostrophe in Thrashin' asks for the dropped G.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is a breed of dog, so an example of a dog-like animal.

clue.text: 'Disco Dancing': hit by famous crooner

parts.note: to club is to hit
Bing Crosby was a famous crooner

explanation.surface: A hit song called Disco Dancing recorded by a celebrated balladeer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a chart success; it is the verb, to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubbing is going to nightclubs to dance, the modern word for a night at the disco.

clue.text: Dogs beginning to trema as grenade explodes round about

indicators.note: explodes round about says the letters are blown apart and scattered into a new order
beginning to picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Dogs start to shake as a grenade goes off nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters T, AS and GRENADE together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Danes are a breed of very large dog.

clue.text: Old boy missing first in English university

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: missing first says the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: Peter is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A former pupil has failed to win a first at an English university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing first' suggests a degree class; it is a deletion of PETER's P.
explanation.definitionFit: The University of Exeter is in Devon, England.

clue.text: Money deducted from wage for industrial action

definitions.meaning: a sum taken off pay before it is paid
a strike, a halt to work

explanation.surface: Pay docked as punishment for a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is both a deduction from pay and a halt in work by strikers.

clue.text: Forecast no member of the family will follow shortened version of broadcast

indicators.note: will follow says the later pieces come after the clipped broadcast
shortened says the word is cut down to its familiar clipped form

parts.note: a broadcast is a programme
taken as written
sis, short for sister, is a member of the family

explanation.surface: A prediction that no relative will watch the abridged edition of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: PROG is the familiar clipping of programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a forecast, especially of how an illness will go.

clue.text: Popular fellow dined without getting drunk

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the scrambled meal goes round the fellow
getting drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man ate a meal and stayed sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking'; here it is the old sense 'outside'. 'getting drunk' rearranges the meal's letters into INDED, which wraps round the fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in demand is sought after, a synonym for well liked.

clue.text: Asian people live among giants

indicators.note: among says one piece stands inside another

parts.note: titans are giants of Greek myth
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Asians dwell alongside huge figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibetans are the people of Tibet in Asia.

clue.text: Rope used by East Lend shipping company?

parts.note: Bow is a district of the East End of London
a line is a shipping company

explanation.surface: A rope used by a London shipping firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally working-class east of London; Bow is one of its districts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowline is a knot, and also the rope running from a sail's edge to the bow.

clue.text: Prisoner given suitable food

parts.note: a con is a convict
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: A convict is served a proper meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Confit is meat such as duck cooked slowly in its own fat, a dish.

clue.text: Soccer final's first nil-n draw

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: each nil is zero, which looks like O
a tie is a draw

explanation.surface: A football final opens in a goalless draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Footie is informal British for football, which Americans call soccer.

clue.text: Converted thus, showing religious education was effective

parts.note: RE is short for religious education, a school subject
worked means was effective

explanation.surface: A conversion achieved because scripture lessons succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reworked has been altered or adapted into a new form.

clue.text: After port, judge is served with a Spanish wine

indicators.note: After says the judge comes behind the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port, often shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: At a harbour a magistrate is given a glass of Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of Spain.

clue.text: Business secured by woman in Italian port

indicators.note: secured by says the first-named piece is held inside the second

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A firm owned by a woman in a harbour in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancona is a port on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Giant conger eel appearing regularly

indicators.note: appearing regularly says every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: An enormous conger eel keeps turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folk tales.

clue.text: with nothing on

annotationWithheld.why: clue held as 'with nothing on (4)', cut short: the definition and the piece giving DID are missing, and there is no scan

clue.text: Monk given time to join us in New Guinea

indicators.note: in says the joined pieces go inside the rearranged country
New suggests a fresh arrangement of the country's letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monk is sent to join a mission in Papua New Guinea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Guinea' reads as the island; 'New' is the anagram signal, rearranging the country's letters into AUGINE, which opens after its third letter to take the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: St Augustine of Canterbury was a Benedictine monk sent to convert the English.

clue.text: Lacking respect, in spite of everything

definitions.meaning: regard is respect, and without it you are ...

explanation.surface: Being disrespectful no matter what.
explanation.definitionFit: Regardless means heedless of something and also nevertheless, anyway.
